question: Does the raw-fusion false-positive leak on the predicted-geometry heldout skew toward OOS rows or toward wrong primary calls?
method: Read-only re-derivation from two persisted audits. No channel rebuild, no new scoring run, no threshold/label/registry change. Canonical masks: 45 primary rows, 83 OOS/secondary rows.

verdict.headline: 46/59 (78%) of raw-fusion confident-wrong calls are OOS-row false positives; 13/59 (22%) are wrong-primary calls. Of the marginal leak fusion introduced over the original hand router (+44 confident-wrong for +8 correct recoveries), 36/44 (82%) is OOS-row FP.
verdict.fork: OOS-concentrated -> channel concordance gating is the indicated fix: require the geometry channel (residue/role/pocket, which survives on predicted backbone) to second a cofactor fire before a primary call. OOS rows match no fingerprint skeleton well, so geometry will not corroborate a lone cofactor fire, which should collapse the OOS leak while preserving the corroborated recoveries. A residual 8-row (incremental) wrong-primary leak remains the target for class-conditional cofactor trust: lean on metal (M-Ionic AUC 0.781), discount weak organic-cofactor calls (heme from 18 training examples, AP 0.53).

limitations.per_fingerprint_attribution_unavailable: The full per-row raw_fused route is not persisted (only the five named target rows plus aggregate canonical-mask counts are). A per-fingerprint breakdown of the 46 OOS / 13 wrong-primary FP cannot be re-derived without rebuilding the cofactor channel and re-running the fusion route.
limitations.channel_rebuild_blocked_in_this_environm: numpy/scipy/sklearn are absent and the ESM-2 embedding sidecars are not persisted in the repo, so the sequence-cofactor channel cannot be rebuilt here without a large model download disallowed by the disk / no-large-download guardrail.
